summary: Agent sandboxes can combine disposable virtual machines, syscall interception, privilege reduction and explicit resource limits. No single mechanism covers isolation, capabilities, cost and audit, so production deployments normally layer them.

items.text: E2B creates isolated on-demand Linux sandboxes for AI agents, exposes filesystem and process APIs, supports templates and lifecycle timeouts, and can discard the environment after the task. It provides a concrete disposable execution boundary for untrusted generated code.

Firecracker's jailer starts a microVM process with a changed root, Linux namespaces, cgroups, dropped privileges and a restricted file-descriptor set. Combined with Firecracker's seccomp filters, it narrows both host exposure and resource access for each execution.

gVisor runs a user-space application kernel that intercepts guest system calls before they reach the host kernel and can add a second isolation layer with platform backends. This is useful where container compatibility is needed but direct host syscall exposure is unacceptable.

Docker rootless mode runs the daemon and containers without root privileges by using a user namespace. It reduces the consequence of a daemon or runtime escape, although it is only one layer and does not by itself impose task-specific capabilities.

Docker resource constraints set CPU, memory and related cgroup limits; the documentation notes that containers otherwise have no resource constraints by default. These controls implement hard cost and denial-of-service bounds around agent execution.
